key_insight: For controlled wake flows, the most compact latent representation is not always the best predictor: POD produces smoother, more forecastable latent dynamics than CAEs, yielding more reliable long-horizon ROMs.
engineering_relevance: For real-time flow control, especially model predictive control and reinforcement learning, choosing a stable latent space can matter more than maximizing compression because forecast robustness directly affects control performance.
method: Compared POD, convolutional autoencoders, and two variational autoencoders for spatial compression.
Used LSTM-based temporal predictors to forecast latent dynamics.
Evaluated two actuated 2D wake cases: a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that CAEs reconstruct short-term fields more sharply and compress better, but their latent trajectories are more irregular and lead to faster degradation and more catastrophic divergence than POD-based models.
watch_item: High compression can hide unstable latent dynamics; in deployment, a model that looks accurate at short horizons may fail abruptly over longer prediction windows.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
